format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.
tools.name: clock

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.
tools.name: sleep

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.
tools.name: collaboration

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.
tools.name: followup_task

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.
tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.
tools.name: list_agents

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 Agent Intelligence is in progress. The existing native runtime now connects a separate Planner, source-bound constraints and bounded memory, observation-informed team proposals, fresh-context independent review and typed durable Agent coordination. One retained strict L1 live run passed with review revision and Worker self-repair, without compaction or restart; the concurrent L2 and later L3 attempts failed. New L2/L3 reruns, complex-task continuity and final frozen-source verification remain pending. The local Provider's small live protocol probes passed [11/11 with the proxy default](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe.json) and [10/11 with explicit `reasoning_effort=none`](docs/audit/phase2/provider-probe-reasoning-none.json); the latter retained a failed exact-text dialogue check. Focused local/Mock suites and exploratory synthetic benchmarks are recorded separately. See the [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md), [status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [architecture decision](docs/adr/ADR-009-agent-intelligence-contracts-and-review.md).

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical recall and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. General autonomous replanning, learned semantic retrieval, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain open. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt

import pytest

from forge_core.domain import DomainError, ModelProfile, Quest
from forge_core.provider_pool import ProviderPool
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.store import Store
from forge_core.team_composition import CompositionLimits, RoleSpec, TeamCompositionService
from forge_core.tool_engine import ToolEngine
from forge_core.worker_runtime import WorkerManager


def prepared_team(tmp_path):
    class MockProvider:
        execution_mode = "mock"

    store = Store(tmp_path / "reassign.sqlite3")
    quest = Quest(title="Partial team", goal="Preserve completed work")
    store.save_quest(quest)
    graph = QuestGraphService(store)
    plan = graph.propose(
        quest.id,
        {
            "nodes": [
                {"key": key, "objective": key, "success_criteria": ["Done"], "budget_tokens": 1000}
                for key in ("a", "b")
            ],
            "edges": [],
            "max_total_tokens": 2000,
        },
        expected_version=0,
    )
    graph.approve(
        quest.id, plan["digest"], plan["revision"], expected_version=1, actor="local_user"
    )
    store.save_model(
        ModelProfile(
            id="m",
            provider="p",
            model_id="m",
            display_name="M",
            context_window=4096,
            max_output_tokens=1000,
        )
    )
    roles = [
        RoleSpec(id=role, task_node_key=key, input_tokens=100, output_tokens=100)
        for role, key in (("coding", "a"), ("reviewer", "b"))
    ]
    limits = CompositionLimits(max_members=2, max_depth=1, max_concurrency=2, max_total_tokens=400)
    service = TeamCompositionService(store)
    team = service.propose(quest.id, roles, limits, strategy="greedy", expected_version=2)
    service.approve(
        quest.id, plan["revision"], team["proposal_digest"], expected_version=2, actor="local_user"
    )
    manager = WorkerManager(
        store, ProviderPool({"p": MockProvider()}), ToolEngine(store), team_authority=service
    )
    for index, key in enumerate(("a", "b")):
        manager.start(
            quest.id, plan["id"], key, team_digest=team["proposal_digest"], member_index=index
        )
    with store.connection() as connection:
        runs = [
            dict(row) for row in connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_runs ORDER BY node_key")
        ]
    return store, quest, plan, roles, limits, service, team, manager, runs


def test_reassignment_preserves_completed_node_and_historical_approval(tmp_path):
    store, quest, plan, roles, limits, service, old, manager, runs = prepared_team(tmp_path)

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from forge_core.domain import Measurement, ModelProfile, PerformanceMeasurement, ProtocolSupport
from forge_core.team_composition import (
    CompositionLimits,
    RoleSpec,
    TeamComposerEngine,
    TeamCompositionService,
    TeamWire,
)


def profile(identity, *, capabilities=None, price=None, currency=None):
    return ModelProfile(
        id=identity,
        provider="provider",
        model_id=identity,
        display_name=identity,
        capabilities=capabilities or {},
        context_window=4096,
        max_output_tokens=512,
        tool_calling_support=ProtocolSupport(supported=True, source="user_override"),
        input_cost_per_million=price,
        output_cost_per_million=price,
        currency=currency,
    )


def test_conflicting_capability_and_performance_sources_are_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        ModelProfile(
            id="m",
            provider="p",
            display_name="M",
            capabilities={"coding": 10},
            capability_measurements={"coding": Measurement(value=90, source="user_override")},
        )
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        ModelProfile(
            id="m",
            provider="p",
            display_name="M",
            reliability=0.1,
            performance_measurements={
                "reliability": PerformanceMeasurement(value=0.9, source="user_override")
            },
        )
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        ModelProfile(
            id="m",
            provider="p",
            display_name="M",
            performance_measurements={
                "timeout_rate": PerformanceMeasurement(value=2, source="user_override")
            },
        )


def test_dynamic_role_requires_complete_bounded_contract():
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        RoleSpec(id="custom", input_tokens=10, output_tokens=10)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        RoleSpec(id="custom", dynamic=True, input_tokens=10, output_tokens=10)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        RoleSpec(
            id="custom",
            dynamic=True,
            input_tokens=10,
            output_tokens=10,
            responsibility="Review",
            input_contract=["input"],
            acceptance_criteria=["Done"],
            output_schema={
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {"x": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["x"],
                "additionalProperties": True,
            },
        )
    role = RoleSpec(
        id="custom",
        dynamic=True,
        input_tokens=10,
        output_tokens=10,
        responsibility="Review output",
        input_contract=["Artifact"],
        acceptance_criteria=["Done"],
        output_schema={
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}},
            "required": ["summary"],
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
    )
    assert role.dynamic and role.output_schema["additionalProperties"] is False


def test_composer_wire_has_closed_required_objects():
    def visit(value):
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            if value.get("type") == "object":
                assert value.get("additionalProperties") is False
                assert set(value.get("required", [])) == set(value.get("properties", {}))
            for child in value.values():
                visit(child)
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            for child in value:
                visit(child)

    visit(TeamWire.model_json_schema())


def test_candidate_audit_excludes_irrelevant_capability_and_uses_known_confidence():
    role = RoleSpec(
        id="coding", required_capabilities={"coding": 70}, input_tokens=100, output_tokens=50

    version = store.get_quest(quest.id)["version"]
    if replacement:

"""Worker checkpoint, budget tables and the delivery contract.

The delivery schema is the default role output contract. Every field except
`summary` is optional with an explicit default so an older, narrower model
response still validates; the Worker prompt asks for all eight, and Core records
which fields the model actually supplied instead of inventing them.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import math
import time
from copy import deepcopy
from decimal import ROUND_CEILING, Decimal
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator

from .domain import DomainError, ForgeEvent, ModelProfile, new_id, now_iso
from .worker_schema import DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA


class RoleSpec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False, revalidate_instances="always")
    id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    task_node_key: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=100)
    required_capabilities: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict, max_length=32)
    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=32)
    input_tokens: int = Field(ge=0, le=1000000)
    output_tokens: int = Field(gt=0, le=1000000)
    max_steps: int = Field(default=8, ge=1, le=32)
    max_tool_calls: int = Field(default=8, ge=0, le=64)
    max_duration_seconds: int = Field(default=60, ge=1, le=3600)
    depth: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, le=8)
    dynamic: bool = False
    responsibility: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=2000)
    input_contract: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
    output_schema: dict | None = None
    acceptance_criteria: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def valid_requirements(self):
        if any(
            not name or not math.isfinite(value) or not 0 <= value <= 100
            for name, value in self.required_capabilities.items()
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid capability requirements")
        if any(not tool for tool in self.tools) or len(set(self.tools)) != len(self.tools):
            raise ValueError("Invalid tool scope")
        if self.id not in PRESET_ROLES and not self.dynamic:
            raise ValueError(
                "Unknown role requires a dynamic proposal; preset IDs are "
                + ", ".join(PRESET_ROLES)
            )
        if any(
            not text.strip() or len(text) > 1000
            for text in [*self.input_contract, *self.acceptance_criteria]
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid role contract")
        if self.dynamic and (
            not self.responsibility
            or not self.responsibility.strip()
            or not self.input_contract
            or not self.output_schema
            or not self.acceptance_criteria
        ):
            raise ValueError("Dynamic role requires a complete contract")
        if self.output_schema is not None:
            _validate_output_schema(self.output_schema)
        return self


class CompositionLimits(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False, revalidate_instances="always")
    max_members: int = Field(ge=1, le=16)
    max_depth: int = Field(ge=0, le=8)
    max_concurrency: int = Field(ge=1, le=16)
    max_total_tokens: int = Field(gt=0, le=16000000)
    max_total_tool_calls: int = Field(default=64, ge=0, le=1024)
    max_cost_microunits: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    currency: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=3, max_length=3, pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}$")
    allowed_tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=32)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_limits(self):
        if self.max_concurrency > self.max_members:
            raise ValueError("Concurrency exceeds member limit")
        if self.max_cost_microunits is not None and self.currency is None:
            raise ValueError("A monetary cap requires an explicit currency")
        if any(not tool for tool in self.allowed_tools) or len(set(self.allowed_tools)) != len(
            self.allowed_tools
        ):
            raise ValueError("Invalid allowed tools")
        return self


PRESET_ROLES = {
    "research": {"research": 70},
    "math": {"mathematics": 70},
    "planner": {"planning": 70},
    "architect": {"architecture": 70},
    "coding": {"coding": 70},
    "design": {"design": 70},
    "experiment": {"coding": 60, "mathematics": 60},
    "reviewer": {"instruction_following": 70},
}

PRESET_RESPONSIBILITIES = {
    "research": "Gather and synthesize relevant evidence.",
    "math": "Develop and check quantitative reasoning.",
    "planner": "Break down objectives and identify dependencies.",
    "architect": "Design system structure and interfaces.",
    "coding": "Implement and inspect the assigned change.",
    "design": "Develop visual and interaction concepts.",
    "experiment": "Design and evaluate reproducible experiments.",
    "reviewer": "Independently examine results and evidence.",
}
# Phase 2 delivery contract (Summary/Findings/Decisions/Artifacts/Evidence/
# Unresolved/Confidence/Next actions). Kept in one place so the Worker prompt,
# the default role contract and the reviewer all describe the same structure.
DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA = DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA


def _validate_output_schema(schema):
    if len(json.dumps(schema, allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")) > 8192:
        raise ValueError("Output schema exceeds size limit")

    def visit(node, depth):
        if not isinstance(node, dict) or depth > 8:
            raise ValueError("Invalid output schema")
        kind = node.get("type")
        if kind == "object":
            if set(node) - {"type", "properties", "required", "additionalProperties"}:
                raise ValueError("Unsupported output schema keyword")
            properties = node.get("properties")
            if (
                not isinstance(properties, dict)
                or len(properties) > 32
                or node.get("additionalProperties") is not False
            ):
                raise ValueError("Output object must be bounded and closed")
            required = node.get("required")
            if (
                not isinstance(required, list)
                or len(set(required)) != len(required)
                or not set(required) <= set(properties)
                or not required
            ):
                raise ValueError("Required output properties must be a subset of the schema")
            # An optional property is only allowed with an explicit bounded default, so a
            # missing value is never ambiguous and never invented by the runtime.
            for name, child in properties.items():
                if name not in set(required) and "default" not in child:
                    raise ValueError("Optional output property requires an explicit default")
            for child in properties.values():
                visit(child, depth + 1)
        elif kind == "array":
            if (
                set(node) - {"type", "items", "maxItems", "default"}
                or type(node.get("maxItems")) is not int
                or not 0 <= node["maxItems"] <= 100
            ):
                raise ValueError("Output arrays require a bounded maxItems")
            visit(node.get("items"), depth + 1)
        elif kind in {"string", "number", "integer", "boolean", "null"}:
            if set(node) - {"type", "default"} or "type" not in node:
                raise ValueError("Unsupported scalar schema keyword")
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported output schema type")

    if schema.get("type") != "object":
        raise ValueError("Output schema root must be an object")
    visit(schema, 0)


class TeamCapabilityWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    name: str
    minimum: float


class TeamRoleWire(BaseModel):
    # Strict Provider schemas require nullable fields to be required. The local
    # parser still accepts omission for compatibility with existing responses.
    model_config = ConfigDict(
        extra="forbid",
        strict=True,
        json_schema_extra=lambda schema: schema.update(required=list(schema["properties"])),
    )
    id: str
    task_node_key: str
    required_capabilities: list[TeamCapabilityWire]
    tools: list[str]
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    max_steps: int
    max_tool_calls: int
    max_duration_seconds: int
    depth: int
    dynamic: bool
    responsibility: str
    input_contract: list[str]
    # Explicit null is a model-selected contract, including for dynamic roles.
    # Local omission retains preset compatibility; it is not a dynamic contract.
    output_schema_json: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Explicit null selects the supplied Core eight-field delivery schema for this role, "
            "including a dynamic role. A dynamic role must still provide nonempty responsibility, "
            "input_contract and acceptance_criteria. A string must contain a valid bounded JSON schema."
        ),
    )
    acceptance_criteria: list[str]


class TeamLimitsWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    max_members: int
    max_depth: int
    max_concurrency: int
    max_total_tokens: int
    max_total_tool_calls: int
    max_cost_microunits: int | None
    currency: str | None
    allowed_tools: list[str]


class TeamWire(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    roles: list[TeamRoleWire]
    limits: TeamLimitsWire
    strategy: Literal["single_model", "greedy", "coverage", "complementarity"]

    def inputs(self):
        roles = []
        for wire in self.roles:
            data = wire.model_dump()
            capabilities = data.pop("required_capabilities")
            if len({item["name"] for item in capabilities}) != len(capabilities):
                raise ValueError("Duplicate capability")
            data["required_capabilities"] = {item["name"]: item["minimum"] for item in capabilities}
            raw_schema = data.pop("output_schema_json")
            if raw_schema is None and "output_schema_json" in wire.model_fields_set:
                data["output_schema"] = deepcopy(DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
            elif raw_schema is None or not raw_schema.strip():
                data["output_schema"] = None
            else:
                if len(raw_schema.encode("utf-8")) > 8192:
                    raise ValueError("Output schema exceeds size limit")
                data["output_schema"] = json.loads(raw_schema)
            roles.append(RoleSpec.model_validate(data))
        return roles, CompositionLimits.model_validate(self.limits.model_dump()), self.strategy


def _cost(profile, role, currency):
    if (
        profile.input_cost_per_million is None
        or profile.output_cost_per_million is None
        or profile.currency is None
        or (currency is not None and profile.currency != currency)
    ):
        return None
    amount = (
        Decimal(str(profile.input_cost_per_million)) * role.input_tokens
        + Decimal(str(profile.output_cost_per_million)) * role.output_tokens
    )
    return int(amount.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING))

    teams = TeamCompositionService(store)

                if name not in set(required) and "default" not in child:
                    raise ValueError("Optional output property requires an explicit default")
            for child in properties.values():

                or type(node.get("maxItems")) is not int
                or not 0 <= node["maxItems"] <= 100
            ):
                raise ValueError("Output arrays require a bounded maxItems")
            visit(node.get("items"), depth + 1)
        elif kind in {"string", "number", "integer", "boolean", "null"}:
            if set(node) - {"type", "default"} or "type" not in node:
                raise ValueError("Unsupported scalar schema keyword")
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported output schema type")

    if schema.get("type") != "object":
        raise ValueError("Output schema root must be an object")

def response(value, *, calls=None):

def delivery(summary="done"):

class ProtocolModel:
    execution_mode = "mock"

    def __init__(self, responses):
        self.responses, self.requests = list(responses), []

        return self.responses.pop(0)

    )

"""Native Composer contracts enforced by real local Worker admission and repair."""

import asyncio
import copy
import json

import jsonschema
import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError
from test_composer_repair_phase2 import team_wire
from test_worker_intelligence_phase2 import ProtocolModel, delivery, response

from forge_core.domain import ModelProfile, Quest
from forge_core.provider_pool import ProviderPool
from forge_core.quest_graph import QuestGraphService
from forge_core.settings import Workspace
from forge_core.store import Store
from forge_core.team_composition import DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA, RoleSpec, TeamCompositionService, TeamWire
from forge_core.tool_engine import ToolEngine
from forge_core.worker_runtime import WorkerManager
from forge_core.worker_schema import DELIVERY_FIELDS, DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA, STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA


def native_worker(tmp_path, responses, *, criterion="Done", contract="native", max_repairs=2):
    store = Store(tmp_path / "core.sqlite3", workspace=Workspace.from_path(tmp_path))
    quest = Quest(title="Native delivery contract", goal="Deliver the approved bounded result")
    store.save_quest(quest)
    graphs = QuestGraphService(store)
    plan = graphs.propose(
        quest.id,
        {
            "nodes": [
                {
                    "key": "n",
                    "objective": quest.goal,
                    "success_criteria": [criterion],
                    "budget_tokens": 60000,
                    "allowed_tools": [],
                }
            ],
            "edges": [],
            "max_total_tokens": 60000,
        },
        expected_version=0,
    )
    graphs.approve(quest.id, plan["digest"], 1, expected_version=1, actor="local_user")
    store.save_model(
        ModelProfile(
            id="protocol",
            provider="protocol",
            model_id="fixture",
            display_name="Offline native contract fixture",
            context_window=64000,
            max_output_tokens=4000,
        )
    )
    proposal = team_wire()
    proposal["roles"][0].update(
        required_capabilities=[],
        input_tokens=30000,
        output_tokens=3000,
        max_steps=6,
        max_duration_seconds=120,
        acceptance_criteria=[criterion],
    )
    proposal["limits"]["max_total_tokens"] = 33000
    if contract == "legacy_string":
        proposal["roles"][0]["output_schema_json"] = json.dumps(DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    roles, limits, strategy = TeamWire.model_validate(proposal).inputs()
    if contract == "legacy_direct":
        roles = [
            RoleSpec(
                id="coding",
                task_node_key="n",
                input_tokens=30000,
                output_tokens=3000,
                max_steps=6,
                max_duration_seconds=120,
            )
        ]
    teams = TeamCompositionService(store)
    team = teams.propose(quest.id, roles, limits, strategy=strategy, expected_version=2)
    teams.approve(quest.id, 1, team["proposal_digest"], expected_version=2, actor="local_user")
    model = ProtocolModel(responses)
    manager = WorkerManager(
        store,
        ProviderPool({"protocol": model}),
        ToolEngine(store),
        team_authority=teams,
        max_repairs=max_repairs,
    )
    worker = manager.start(
        quest.id, plan["id"], "n", team_digest=team["proposal_digest"], member_index=0
    )
    return store, manager, model, worker, team


def test_native_schema_is_separate_from_unchanged_legacy_default():
    assert DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA is DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA
    assert DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["required"] == ["summary"]
    assert STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["required"] == list(DELIVERY_FIELDS)
    assert STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["properties"]["confidence"]["minimum"] == 0
    assert STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["properties"]["confidence"]["maximum"] == 1
    assert "minimum" not in DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["properties"]["confidence"]
    assert STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["properties"] is not DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA["properties"]
    jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.check_schema(STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    jsonschema.validate({"summary": "old contract"}, DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("field", DELIVERY_FIELDS)
def test_native_schema_requires_each_model_supplied_field_without_default_insertion(field):
    value = delivery()
    del value[field]
    before = copy.deepcopy(value)
    with pytest.raises(jsonschema.ValidationError):
        jsonschema.validate(value, STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    assert value == before and field not in value


@pytest.mark.parametrize("confidence", [0, 0.8, 1])
def test_native_schema_accepts_confidence_bounds(confidence):
    value = delivery()
    value["confidence"] = confidence
    jsonschema.validate(value, STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("confidence", [-0.01, 1.01, True, "0.8", None])
def test_native_schema_rejects_invalid_confidence(confidence):
    value = delivery()
    value["confidence"] = confidence
    with pytest.raises(jsonschema.ValidationError):
        jsonschema.validate(value, STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "criterion",
    ["Done", "json_review:work/report.json", "numeric_self_test:work/code.py", "delivery_review"],
)
def test_native_worker_rejects_summary_then_repairs_complete_delivery_for_any_criterion(
    tmp_path, criterion
):
    store, manager, model, worker, team = native_worker(
        tmp_path, [response({"summary": "incomplete"}), response(delivery())], criterion=criterion
    )
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert team["members"][0]["output_schema"] == STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    assert result["steps"] == 2 and result["token_spent"] == 80
    feedback = json.loads(model.requests[1].messages[-1]["content"])["repair_request"]
    assert feedback["reason_code"] == "invalid_output_contract"
    assert feedback["detail"]["schema"] == "output_schema"
    events = store.list_events(limit=100)
    accepted = [event for event in events if event["event_type"] == "worker.result"]
    assert len(accepted) == 1
    payload = json.loads(accepted[0]["payload"])
    assert json.loads(payload["claim"]) == delivery()
    assert payload["delivery_fields_supplied"] == list(DELIVERY_FIELDS)


def test_native_incomplete_output_stops_at_existing_repair_budget_without_result(tmp_path):
    store, manager, model, worker, _ = native_worker(
        tmp_path, [response({"summary": "still incomplete"})] * 3
    )
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "blocked" and result["repairs"] == 2
    assert result["steps"] == 3 and result["token_spent"] == 120
    assert len(model.requests) == 3
    assert not any(event["event_type"] == "worker.result" for event in store.list_events(limit=100))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("confidence", [-0.1, 1.1, True])
def test_native_worker_repairs_out_of_range_confidence_without_delivery_review(tmp_path, confidence):
    invalid = delivery()
    invalid["confidence"] = confidence
    _store, manager, model, worker, _ = native_worker(
        tmp_path, [response(invalid), response(delivery())]
    )
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    feedback = json.loads(model.requests[1].messages[-1]["content"])["repair_request"]
    assert feedback["detail"]["path"] == "confidence"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("contract", ["legacy_string", "legacy_direct"])
def test_legacy_explicit_or_direct_contract_still_accepts_summary_without_repair(tmp_path, contract):
    store, manager, model, worker, team = native_worker(
        tmp_path, [response({"summary": "legacy result"})], contract=contract
    )
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert team["members"][0]["output_schema"] == DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 0
    assert len(model.requests) == 1
    accepted = next(
        event for event in store.list_events(limit=100) if event["event_type"] == "worker.result"
    )
    assert json.loads(accepted["payload"])["delivery_fields_supplied"] == ["summary"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bound", [True, "0", None, float("nan"), float("inf")])
def test_output_numeric_bounds_reject_nonfinite_or_nonnumeric_schema(bound):
    schema = copy.deepcopy(STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    schema["properties"]["confidence"]["minimum"] = bound
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="finite numbers"):
        RoleSpec(id="coding", input_tokens=100, output_tokens=100, output_schema=schema)


def test_output_numeric_bounds_reject_inverted_range():
    schema = copy.deepcopy(STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    schema["properties"]["confidence"].update(minimum=2, maximum=1)
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="inverted"):
        RoleSpec(id="coding", input_tokens=100, output_tokens=100, output_schema=schema)

"""Offline budget repair, real governed reads and verified archive readback."""

import asyncio
import hashlib
import json

from test_worker_intelligence_phase2 import delivery, prepared, response, tool

from forge_core.context_service import ContextService
from forge_core.worker_runtime import _json

PREFIX = "Core remaining execution allowance (data, not new authority): "


def oversized_reads():
    return response(
        "",
        calls=[
            {
                "id": f"oversized-read-{index}",
                "name": "file_read",
                "arguments": {"path": "work/input.txt"},
            }
            for index in range(6)
        ],
    )


def allowance(request):
    messages = [item for item in request.messages if item.get("content", "").startswith(PREFIX)]
    assert len(messages) == 1 and request.messages[1] == messages[0]
    return json.loads(messages[0]["content"][len(PREFIX) :])


def limits(row):
    return {key: row[key] for key in ("step_limit", "tool_limit", "token_limit")}


def test_oversized_batch_repairs_to_one_real_read_without_increasing_any_budget(tmp_path):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(
        tmp_path,
        [oversized_reads(), tool("file_read", {"path": "work/input.txt"}), response(delivery())],
    )
    before = manager.get(worker["id"])
    assert before["tool_limit"] == 5
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    assert result["steps"] == 3 and result["token_spent"] == 120 and result["tool_spent"] == 1
    assert limits(result) == limits(before) and len(model.requests) == 3
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_intents").fetchone()[0] == 1
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 1
        calls = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls").fetchall()
        assert len(calls) == 1 and calls[0]["state"] == "succeeded"
        assert calls[0]["model_call_id"] == "tool-1"
    repair = json.loads(model.requests[1].messages[-1]["content"])["repair_request"]
    assert repair["reason_code"] == "tool_batch_budget"
    assert repair["detail"] == {"remaining_tool_calls": 5, "requested_tool_calls": 6}
    assert "Original source" == json.loads(model.requests[-1].messages[-1]["content"])["content"]


def test_repeated_oversized_batches_stop_at_original_repair_bound_without_actions(tmp_path):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, [oversized_reads() for _ in range(3)])
    before = manager.get(worker["id"])
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "blocked" and result["repairs"] == manager.max_repairs == 2
    assert result["steps"] == 3 and result["token_spent"] == 120 and result["tool_spent"] == 0
    assert limits(result) == limits(before) and len(model.requests) == 3
    with store.connection() as connection:
        for table in ("worker_tool_calls", "action_intents", "action_receipts"):
            assert connection.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {table}").fetchone()[0] == 0
    blocked = [
        json.loads(event["payload"])
        for event in store.list_events(limit=100)
        if event["event_type"] == "worker.blocked"
    ]
    assert blocked[-1]["reason_code"] == "tool_budget"


def test_each_request_reports_current_allowance_and_reserves_complete_feedback_json(tmp_path):
    _store, manager, model, worker = prepared(
        tmp_path,
        [oversized_reads(), tool("file_read", {"path": "work/input.txt"}), response(delivery())],
    )
    original_generate = model.generate
    observed = []

    async def inspect_reservation(request):
        current = manager.get(worker["id"])
        feedback = allowance(request)
        settled_spent = 40 * len(observed)
        assert feedback["remaining_cumulative_tokens"] == current["token_limit"] - settled_spent
        assert feedback["remaining_model_steps"] == current["step_limit"] - len(observed)
        assert feedback["remaining_tool_calls"] == current["tool_limit"] - current["tool_spent"]
        complete_input = len(
            _json(
                {"messages": request.messages, "tools": request.tools, "model": request.model_id}
            ).encode()
        )
        reservation = complete_input + request.max_output_tokens + 64 + 16 * len(request.messages)
        assert current["token_spent"] == settled_spent + reservation
        assert reservation <= request.context_limit
        assert current["token_spent"] <= current["token_limit"]
        without_feedback = [item for index, item in enumerate(request.messages) if index != 1]
        smaller_input = len(
            _json(
                {"messages": without_feedback, "tools": request.tools, "model": request.model_id}
            ).encode()
        )
        assert complete_input > smaller_input + len(PREFIX.encode())
        observed.append(feedback)
        return await original_generate(request)

    model.generate = inspect_reservation
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending"
    assert [item["remaining_tool_calls"] for item in observed] == [5, 5, 4]
    assert [item["remaining_model_steps"] for item in observed] == [12, 11, 10]
    assert [item["remaining_cumulative_tokens"] for item in observed] == [33000, 32960, 32920]


def test_archive_guidance_points_to_a_real_available_verified_source_tool(tmp_path):
    store, manager, model, worker = prepared(
        tmp_path,
        [
            tool("worker_read_context_source", {"ordinal": 2, "max_chars": 2048}),
            response(delivery()),
        ],
    )
    # Explicit synthetic history isolates archive/source integrity; it is never
    # represented as a real-provider task or an execution receipt.
    original = {"role": "assistant", "content": "Original archived source 中文 \\" * 300}
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        for ordinal in range(2, 6):
            work.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (worker["id"], ordinal, "assistant", _json(original)),
            )
        for ordinal in (6, 7):
            work.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (
                    worker["id"],
                    ordinal,
                    "assistant",
                    _json({"role": "assistant", "content": "next"}),
                ),
            )
    context = ContextService(store)
    context.build_worker_context(worker["id"], input_budget=10000)
    assert json.loads(context.read_source("worker", worker["id"], 2)["message_json"]) == original
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["tool_spent"] == 1
    request = model.requests[0]
    assert "worker_read_context_source" in allowance(request)["instruction"]
    assert "worker_read_context_source" in {item["name"] for item in request.tools}
    archived = next(
        item for item in request.messages if item.get("content", "").startswith("Archived task")
    )
    capsule = json.loads(archived["content"].split(": ", 1)[1])
    assert any("2" in item["source_refs"] for item in capsule["hypotheses"])
    returned = json.loads(model.requests[-1].messages[-1]["content"])
    assert returned["source_sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(_json(original).encode()).hexdigest()
    assert returned["content"] == _json(original)[:2048]
    assert returned["next_offset_chars"] == 2048 and returned["complete"] is False
    assert allowance(model.requests[-1])["remaining_tool_calls"] == 4
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_intents").fetchone()[0] == 0
        call = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_tool_calls").fetchone()
        assert call["tool_name"] == "worker_read_context_source" and call["state"] == "succeeded"
"""Compact publisher tests; no credentials, Providers or actual live runs used."""

import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


@pytest.fixture
def publisher():
    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts/phase2/publish_evidence.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("phase2_publisher_tests", path)
    result = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(result)
    return result


def synthetic_record():
    return {
        "run_id": "synthetic-run",
        "level": "L2",
        "execution_mode": "live",
        "prompt": "SECRET_SENTINEL",
        "core_log_tail": "SECRET_SENTINEL",
        "router_turn": {"reply": "SECRET_SENTINEL", "status": 200},
        "failures": ["planner_did_not_produce_plan"],
        "execution": {
            "final_status": "awaiting_approval",
            "cost": None,
            "token_usage": {"input": 15, "output": 3, "unknown_attempts": 1},
            "review_results": [{"verdict": "BLOCKED", "findings": ["SECRET_SENTINEL"]}],
            "artifact_hashes": [
                {
                    "path": "C:/private/account/work/report.json",
                    "sha256": "a" * 64,
                    "receipt_hash_matches": True,
                }
            ],
        },
    }


def test_compaction_omits_all_free_content_and_private_absolute_paths(publisher):
    compact = publisher.compact_record(synthetic_record())
    text = json.dumps(compact)
    assert "SECRET_SENTINEL" not in text
    assert "private/account" not in text
    assert compact["artifact_hashes"][0]["path"] == "work/report.json"
    assert compact["cost"] is None
    assert compact["token_usage"]["unknown_attempts"] == 1
    assert compact["actual_final_status"] == "awaiting_approval"


def test_publication_keeps_measured_retries_and_fixed_review_reason_only(publisher):
    record = synthetic_record()
    record["execution"].update(
        retry_count=4,
        retry_breakdown={
            "worker_self_repairs": 2,
            "review_revision_requests": 1,
            "credential": "SECRET_SENTINEL",
        },
        review_results=[
            {
                "verdict": "BLOCKED",
                "reason_code": "review_context_limit",
                "findings": ["SECRET_SENTINEL"],
            }
        ],
    )
    compact = publisher.compact_record(record)
    assert compact["retry_count"] == 4
    assert compact["retry_breakdown"]["worker_self_repairs"] == 2
    assert compact["retry_breakdown"]["review_revision_requests"] == 1
    assert compact["review_results"][0]["reason_code"] == "review_context_limit"
    assert "SECRET_SENTINEL" not in json.dumps(compact)


def test_publication_hashes_exact_source_and_output_without_overwriting(tmp_path, publisher):
    source = tmp_path / "runs"
    run = source / "synthetic-run"
    run.mkdir(parents=True)
    raw = json.dumps(synthetic_record()).encode()
    (run / "run.json").write_bytes(raw)
    target = tmp_path / "publication"
    index = publisher.publish_runs(source, target)
    entry = index["runs"][0]
    assert entry["source_snapshot"]["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
    publication = (target / entry["published_snapshot"]["path"]).read_bytes()
    assert entry["published_snapshot"]["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(publication).hexdigest()
    assert entry["failures"] == ["planner_did_not_produce_plan"]
    with pytest.raises(FileExistsError):
        publisher.publish_runs(source, target)
    assert (run / "run.json").read_bytes() == raw


def test_empty_source_does_not_publish_a_fake_empty_evidence_set(tmp_path, publisher):
    source = tmp_path / "runs"
    source.mkdir()
    target = tmp_path / "publication"
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No finished"):
        publisher.publish_runs(source, target)
    assert not target.exists()


def test_identifier_fields_cannot_smuggle_auth_tokens_or_urls(publisher):
    record = synthetic_record()
    record["failures"].append("sk-synthetic-not-a-real-key")
    record["execution"]["model_attempts"] = [

class TaskNodeProposal(BaseModel):

    @model_validator(mode="after")

        from .tool_domain import CONTRACTS

        return self

class GraphProposal(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    nodes: list[TaskNodeProposal] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    edges: list[TaskEdgeProposal] = Field(max_length=512)
    max_total_tokens: int = Field(default=1000000, ge=1, le=1000000)
    max_cost_microunits: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    cost_currency: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=r"^[A-Z]{3}$")
    max_duration_seconds: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def graph_valid(self):
        if (self.max_cost_microunits is None) != (self.cost_currency is None):
            raise ValueError("A cost limit requires an explicit currency")
        keys = [node.key for node in self.nodes]
        if (
            len(keys) != len(set(keys))
            or sum(node.budget_tokens for node in self.nodes) > self.max_total_tokens
        ):
            raise ValueError("Duplicate node or total budget exceeded")
        incoming = dict.fromkeys(keys, 0)
        outgoing = {key: [] for key in keys}
        edges = set()
        for edge in self.edges:
            pair = (edge.source, edge.target)
            if edge.source not in incoming or edge.target not in incoming or pair in edges:
                raise ValueError("Invalid graph edge")
            edges.add(pair)
            incoming[edge.target] += 1
            outgoing[edge.source].append(edge.target)
        ready = [key for key, count in incoming.items() if count == 0]
        count = 0
        while ready:
            node = ready.pop()
            count += 1
            for child in outgoing[node]:
                incoming[child] -= 1
                if incoming[child] == 0:
                    ready.append(child)
        if count != len(keys):
            raise ValueError("Graph contains a cycle")
        return self

    """Check all declared requirements in the caller's completion transaction.

    def __init__(self, store, *, verify_model_run=None):

    def check(self, work, quest):

            "SELECT * FROM quest_plans WHERE quest_id=? AND revision=? AND status='approved'",
            (quest["id"], quest["plan_revision"]),

                "SELECT * FROM task_nodes WHERE plan_id=? ORDER BY node_key", (plan["id"],)
            ).fetchall()

            for node in nodes:
                if node["status"] == "succeeded":
                    self._check_live_node(work, quest, plan, node)
                elif node["status"] == "failed":
                    self._check_failed_node(work, quest, plan, node)
                    recovery = work.connection.execute(
                        "SELECT target FROM task_edges WHERE plan_id=? AND source=? AND condition='failure'",
                        (plan["id"], node["node_key"]),
                    ).fetchall()
                    if not any(
                        states[edge["target"]]["status"] == "succeeded" for edge in recovery
                    ):
                        raise DomainError("Failed task has no verified recovery")
                elif node["status"] == "skipped":
                    self._check_skipped_node(work, quest, plan, node, states, set())
                else:
                    raise DomainError("Every task requires independent verification")
            requirements = work.connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM quest_requirements WHERE quest_id=?", (quest["id"],)
            ).fetchone()
            if requirements is not None:
                if requirements["plan_revision"] != quest["plan_revision"]:
                    raise DomainError("Current requirements are required")
                try:
                    approvals = json.loads(requirements["required_approvals_json"])
                    if not isinstance(approvals, list) or any(
                        not isinstance(item, str) for item in approvals
                    ):
                        raise ValueError
                except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
                    raise DomainError("Invalid completion requirements") from exc
                for approval_id in approvals:
                    action = work.connection.execute(
                        """SELECT a.* FROM action_intents a JOIN action_receipts r ON r.intent_id=a.id
                        WHERE a.approval_id=? AND a.quest_id=? AND a.plan_revision=? AND a.state='succeeded'
                        AND a.execution_mode='live' AND r.execution_mode='live'""",
                        (approval_id, quest["id"], quest["plan_revision"]),
                    ).fetchone()
                    approval = work.connection.execute(
                        "SELECT * FROM approvals WHERE id=?", (approval_id,)
                    ).fetchone()
                    if (
                        action is None
                        or approval is None
                        or not _approval_valid(dict(approval), quest)
                    ):
                        raise DomainError("Required approval lacks a verified action receipt")
            return
        row = work.connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM quest_requirements WHERE quest_id=?", (quest["id"],)

        try:

            approvals = json.loads(row["required_approvals_json"])
            if (

        runs = work.connection.execute(

def test_planner_invalid_tools_after_repair_leave_no_plan_or_worker(tmp_path):
    store = Store(tmp_path / "failed-plan-repair.sqlite3")
    quest = Quest(title="Inspect", goal="Inspect safely")

    invalid = wire_graph()
    invalid["nodes"][0]["allowed_tools"] = ["execute_arbitrary_shell"]

@pytest.mark.parametrize(

def test_planner_repairs_artifact_criteria_without_own_write_permission(tmp_path, criterion):
    store = Store(tmp_path / "artifact-plan.sqlite3")
    quest = Quest(title="Artifact task", goal="Create a governed artifact")
    store.save_quest(quest)
    invalid = wire_graph()
    invalid["nodes"][0]["success_criteria"] = [criterion]
    valid = copy.deepcopy(invalid)
    valid["nodes"][0]["allowed_tools"] += ["file_write", "file_revise"]
    provider = ScriptedMock(invalid, valid)
    plan = generate(store, quest, provider)
    assert len(provider.requests) == 2
    assert (
        "Artifact criteria require file_write on the same node"
        in provider.requests[1].messages[-1]["content"]
    )
    assert plan["nodes"][0]["success_criteria"] == [criterion]
    assert "file_write" in plan["nodes"][0]["allowed_tools"]
    assert len(QuestGraphService(store).history(quest.id)) == 1

        """
        token = secrets.token_hex(24)

        with self.store.unit_of_work() as work:
            work.connection.execute("""INSERT OR IGNORE INTO node_verification_attempts(plan_id,node_key,worker_id)
                SELECT n.plan_id,n.node_key,n.worker_id FROM task_nodes n JOIN quest_plans p ON p.id=n.plan_id
                JOIN quests q ON q.id=p.quest_id WHERE n.status='review_pending' AND n.worker_id IS NOT NULL
                AND q.status='running' AND p.status='approved' AND p.revision=q.plan_revision""")
            work.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE node_verification_attempts SET state='blocked',claim_token=NULL,error_code='attempts_exhausted' WHERE state='checking' AND next_attempt<=? AND attempts>=3",
                (now,),
            )
            candidates = work.connection.execute(
                """SELECT v.*,p.quest_id FROM node_verification_attempts v
                JOIN task_nodes n ON n.plan_id=v.plan_id AND n.node_key=v.node_key AND n.worker_id=v.worker_id
                JOIN quest_plans p ON p.id=v.plan_id JOIN quests q ON q.id=p.quest_id
                WHERE v.state IN ('pending','checking') AND v.attempts<3 AND v.next_attempt<=?
                AND n.status='review_pending' AND q.status='running' AND p.status='approved' AND p.revision=q.plan_revision
                ORDER BY v.attempts,v.next_attempt,v.plan_id,v.node_key LIMIT 64""",
                (now,),
            ).fetchall()
            row = None

                    "SELECT criteria_json FROM task_nodes WHERE plan_id=? AND node_key=?",

                selected = review_criteria(json.loads(node[0]))

                    run = work.connection.execute(

                    ).fetchone()
                    if run is None or not all(
                        review_pass_matches(self.store, work.connection, run, item)
                        for item in selected
                    ):
                        continue
                row = candidate
                break
            if row is None:
                return False
            work.connection.execute(
                "UPDATE node_verification_attempts SET attempts=attempts+1,state='checking',next_attempt=?,claim_token=REDACTED WHERE plan_id=? AND node_key=? AND worker_id=?",
